title: A third objection: God 'expected' grapes and got wild grapes (Isaiah 5)
source_text: XII. Imo Scriptura docere videtur quaedam aliter contingere quam Deus ipse conjecerit, quandoquidem affirmat quaedam ab hominibus fieri, contra quam ipse expectarat. Ut quum Deus ita de contumacia & rebellione populi Judaici queritur, Quid est quod debui ultra facere vineae meae, & non feci ei? Cur expectavi ut faceret uvas, & fecit labruscas? apud Isaiam cap. quinto.
pass_a_gloss: Nay Scripture seems to teach that some things happen otherwise than God himself had conjectured, since it affirms that some things are done by men, contrary to what he himself had expected. As when God thus complains of the stubbornness and rebellion of the Jewish people, What is there that I ought to have done more to my vineyard, and have not done to it? Why did I expect that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes? in Isaiah chap. five.
pass_b_english: Scripture even seems to teach that some things turn out otherwise than God himself had supposed, since it says that people do some things contrary to what he had expected.

So God complains of the stubbornness and rebellion of the Jewish people in Isaiah 5: 'What more should I have done for my vineyard that I have not done? Why, when I expected it to yield grapes, did it yield wild grapes?'

lemmas.gloss: contrary to what he himself had expected

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
